capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction.

- For the Bernoulli measure identity, use its representation as the convex combination of Dirac measures at \(x\) and \(y\). Apply the measurable-set evaluation formula using `hs`, then split into the four cases \(x\in s\)/\(x\notin s\) and \(y\in s\)/\(y\notin s\). Dirac measures evaluate to \(0\) or \(1\), giving respectively \(1\), \(p\), \(1-p\) (represented by `unitInterval.symm p`), or \(0\), exactly matching the nested `ite`.

- For the geometric statement, establish a positive uniform separation between the compact set \(s\) and the disjoint closed set \(t\). Closedness gives, for every point of \(s\), a positive-radius neighborhood avoiding \(t\); compactness extracts a finite subcover and hence a common positive radius. Choose \(\delta\) smaller than half this separation. If a point belonged to both thickenings, it would be within \(\delta\) of each set, and the triangle inequality would produce points of \(s\) and \(t\) closer than the separation, a contradiction.

The closedness of \(t\) and compactness of \(s\) are essential: disjoint arbitrary sets can have distance zero, in which case no positive-radius disjoint thickenings exist.
